correctness.rationale: For smooth plane quartics over odd finite fields, odd theta characteristics correspond Galois-equivariantly to the 28 bitangents (hyperflexes included). In symplectic F2 coordinates the quadratic refinements Q_t are odd iff Q0(t)=1; six basis-vector tests Q0(Me_j)+B(t,Me_j+e_j)=0 exactly characterize fixed refinements, while dim ker(M-I) is the rational two-torsion rank. All Sp6(F2) matrices correspond to ordered symplectic bases: (63)(32)(15)(8)(3)(2)=1451520, so the enumeration is exhaustive over the group, not an experiment on selected plane quartics. The independent C enumeration built from the checked basis symplectic conditions enumerated all 1451520 elements and reproduced each of the 18 (r,b,multiplicity) table entries exactly. For fixed ranks r>=4, a zero restricted quadratic form would create an impossible totally isotropic subspace of dimension >3; at r=3 the Lagrangian shear must be an alternating odd-dimensional singular matrix, giving a fourth fixed vector. A nonconstant degree-at-most-two Boolean polynomial on r fixed dimensions has weight at least 2^(r-2), so b>=2^(r-2) when r>=3; the complete table sharpens rank 5/6. No arithmetic realization of every abstract row is deduced.
residual_risks: Classical Galois-equivariant odd theta/bitangent correspondence is an invoked standard theorem, not derived from first principles.
Counts are exact symplectic-element multiplicities, not weighted finite-field quartic counts or a proof of geometric realizability for all rows.

value.rationale: Rational two-torsion is a natural visible arithmetic invariant of genus-three Jacobians, and rational bitangents are their classical theta-geometric counterparts. The exact 18-row joint action census and rank-conditioned minimums permit precise constraints on every smooth plane quartic over odd finite fields. It is not a user-chosen arbitrary small slice: it exhausts the full canonical Sp6(F2) action and distinguishes geometric necessity from curve realizability; an arithmetic geometer can use the table to rule out inconsistent Frobenius/bitangent observations.
